newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran cleric questions legitimacy of Algerian polls.
newsitem.headline: Iran cleric questions legitimacy of Algerian polls.

text.p: A senior Iranian cleric on Friday said Algeria's election, held by the authorities without the country's main Islamist group, were illegal.

"They have gone to great lengths to prepare for the election and provide security for it, and they have banned the Islamic Salvation Front (FIS)," head of judiciary Ayatollah Mohammad Yazdi said in a prayer sermon carried by Tehran radio.

"They have said 'You (FIS) cannot participate in the elections.' Can you call that an election?," Yazdi told thousands of worshippers gathered at the mausoleum of late Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini who led Iran's 1979 Islamic revolution.

"Five years ago there was an election and we all know that the Islamic Salvation Front won, but global arrogance (the West) trampled on the obvious rights of the Islamic Salvation Front... and brought to power a dictatorial government," Yazdi said.
"Those who dominate the country and direct it along their arrogant (Western) guidelines...what kind of people are they? They are killing so many people to save their government," he added.

Iran has repeatedly called for talks between Algeria's government and opposition groups to end the violence which flared after the Algerian authorities in January 1992 scrapped a general election dominated by the Islamic Salvation Front (FIS).
An estimated 60,000 people have been killed in the violence.
The FIS is outlawed and new laws bar the use of Islam as a political platform, ensuring no other party could provide an alternative.
Algeria cut diplomatic relations with Iran in 1993 over what it called Iranian backing for Moslem militants fighting the secular government.
Tehran says it only gives moral and political support to Islamic movements such as those in Algeria, which it says are inspired by the Iranian revolution.

Algeria's Interior Ministry said the pro-presidential National Democratic Party won 155 of 380 seats in parliament, ahead of the Islam-oriented Movement of a Peaceful Society (MPS) which received 69 seats in the Thursday polls. The MPS complained of vote irregularities.
